problems.title: False scaled determinant estimate and fixed-base Hessian formulas in Proposition6.7
problems.claim: For all beta in[0,1] and sufficiently small alpha, det(alpha^2 Ric|span{U,F2})>1/2.
problems.parameters: Even k=2, beta=1, psi=pi/2, arbitrary alpha>0. Separate Hessian check k=2,beta=1/2,psi=pi/4.
assumptions_verified: Metric and orthonormal frame are the actual family of equations(97)–(99)
problems.actual_result: The true two-by-two block has A=2, B=2alpha k/sqrt(1+alpha^2k^2), C=(alpha^-2+2alpha^2k^2)/(1+alpha^2k^2). Scaled determinant=2alpha^2/(1+alpha^2k^2); for k2 it is always<1/2 and equals1/52 at alpha1/10. The actual Hessian F2/u is c^2 cos^2/(u^2 f^2), not c^2 cos^2/u^4, because the base uses k rather than c=(1-beta)k.
problems.impact: The decisive positivity computation in the central twisting construction uses a false quantitative assertion and incorrect exact derivatives. This damages the displayed proof step; it does not disprove positive Ricci curvature or Proposition6.7.
problems.correction: Correct the fixed-base derivatives. Use the Schur complement of Ric-I: with q=(1-beta)k sin(psi), A=2+q^2+O_k(alpha^2), alpha B=-q+O_k(alpha^2), alpha^2 C=1+O_k(alpha^2). The Schur complement tends uniformly to1.
problems.repair_verification: Independent symbolic algebra verifies the corrected component formulas and the Schur-complement limit1. Compactness and denominators f,u>=1 give the uniform local repair, conditional on the remaining stated base/connection formulas. Other gluing stages not thereby certified.

problems.title: Coprimality does not ensure freeness of the stated circle action
problems.claim: The (a,b) circle action is free whenever gcd(a,b)=1 and a!=0.
problems.parameters: (a,b)=(2,1), theta=pi, any S3 point and a pole of the S2 cross-section in the prescribed product end.
assumptions_verified: Point is in the stipulated end geometry
problems.actual_result: The Hopf factor e^{ia theta}=1 and the S2 pole is fixed, producing a nontrivial stabilizer.
problems.impact: The stated auxiliary generality is false. The induction explicitly uses (1,k) and (1,0), whose first Hopf weight is1, so this does not obstruct its actual freeness requirement.
problems.correction: Restrict the freeness assertion to a=+/-1, or describe the stabilizers for other weights.
problems.repair_verification: The product end makes |a|=1 necessary; the globally free first Hopf action makes it sufficient.

problems.title: Exact volume exponents cannot hold for every positive eta
problems.claim: For every eta>0 there are unbounded radii t_i with Vol(B_ti)=t_i^(3+eta).
problems.parameters: eta=4 in a complete dimension6 manifold with Ric>=0.
assumptions_verified: The dimension and curvature assumptions are exactly those of Theorem1.1 invoked in Proposition4.4
problems.actual_result: Radial Jacobi comparison gives Vol(B_t)<=omega6 t^6, omega6=pi^3/6. Thus t^7 equality is impossible for t>omega6, and cannot occur along t_i->infinity.
problems.impact: Overstated auxiliary equality/quantifier. The main theorem asks for upper/lower inequalities; restricting the construction proposition to small eta supplies the large-eta inequalities by monotonicity at radii>=1.
problems.correction: State the exact-equality proposition for sufficiently small eta, for example0<eta<1; use eta0<min(eta,1) for the theorem's weaker inequalities.
problems.repair_verification: Necessary-bound contradiction and reduction of the main inequalities verified. Existence of all small-eta sequences still depends on the construction.

problem_reviews.claim: The auxiliary eta in the proof of Lemma3.3 is asserted to satisfy incompatible prescribed values on overlapping regions.
problem_reviews.definitions_quantifiers_hypotheses: Source pages14-15 place centres x^a on the sphere of radius r_(j+1)/10 in a rotation orbit, with disjoint A_(r_j,2r_j)(x^a), origin outside each annulus and r_(j+1)>>r_j>>1. Property(a) specifies |x-x^0|^2 on the first annulus; property(c) visibly specifies |x|^2 outside B_(100 r_j)(0), with subscript j. The function domain excludes only the inner balls.
problem_reviews.decisive_evidence: Choose r_j=100, r_(j+1)=1000000, k_(j+1)=2, x^0=(100000,0,0), x^1=(-100000,0,0), and x=(100150,0,0). A rotation by pi exchanges the centres, whose distance200000 exceeds4r_j. The test point is150 from x^0, outside all inner balls and outside B_10000(0). Direct primary arithmetic gives22500 versus10030022500, a difference10030000000. More generally x=x^0+1.5r_j e1 works whenever r_(j+1)/r_j>1000, so stronger required scale separation cannot cure the conflict. No smoothness or critical-point assumption is needed to derive this inconsistency.
problem_reviews.source_location: Source PDF pages14-15; actual page15 properties(a),(c), and page14 Lemma3.3 with the explicit deduction of Proposition3.1.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependencies: The construction concerns a freely chosen auxiliary function and may admit a corrected outer scale. This does not produce a different topology for the limiting manifold or contradict existence of a Ricci-nonnegative Milnor example. Nevertheless the written function cannot exist, and Lemma3.3 is explicitly the route to the compatible proper Morse-Bott exhaustion and universal-cover diffeomorphism.
problem_reviews.impact: Major proof defect in the stated core topological conclusion's proof, with main existence not refuted.
problem_reviews.repair_and_limits: An outer matching region enclosing the annuli, depending on r_(j+1), removes the displayed overlap only. A full repair must still establish affine matching at other holes, absence of positive-level critical points, compatibility with earlier f_j, and the properness lower bound. These are not verified merely by changing a radius index.

problem_reviews.claim: The determinant bound for alpha^2 Ric at the end of Proposition6.7 is false in the stipulated metric family, and the intermediate F2 Hessian/Laplacian formulas incorrectly change the fixed base.
problem_reviews.definitions_quantifiers_hypotheses: Theorem2.2 permits even k=2. Proposition6.7 permits beta in[0,1] and all sufficiently small positive alpha; psi=pi/2 is regular. Pages29-30 explicitly keep(N,h^alpha) fixed with f^2=1+alpha^2 k^2 sin^2(psi), while changing fibre length u^2=1+alpha^2 c^2 sin^2(psi), c=(1-beta)k, and interpolating the connection. The frame is the actual orthonormal frame(99).
problem_reviews.decisive_evidence: At beta=1, u=1, its Hessian vanishes, omega=-2 Z2* wedge Z3* has no F2 contraction, and div omega(F2)=-4alpha k/f at psi=pi/2. Equations(60)-(62),(90),(95),(104) therefore give A=2, B=2alpha k/f, C=(alpha^-2+2alpha^2 k^2)/f^2. The primary executor derived det(alpha^2 R)=alpha^4(AC-B^2)=2alpha^2/(1+alpha^2 k^2). For k=2 its gap below1/2 is1/[2(1+4alpha^2)]>0 for every alpha>0; at alpha=1/10 the value is1/52. Thus choosing a smaller alpha threshold cannot repair the printed assertion.
problem_reviews.hessian_rederivation: The base S2 fibre is totally geodesic and has meridian element alpha dpsi and rotational profile a=alpha sin(psi)/f, also confirmed by frame(123). Hence a'/a=cos(psi)/(sin(psi)f^2), u'=alpha^2 c^2 sin(psi)cos(psi)/u, and Hess(u)(F2,F2)/u=c^2 cos^2(psi)/(u^2 f^2). The printed denominator is u^4. Actual minus printed is -alpha^2 c^2(k^2-c^2)sin^2(psi)cos^2(psi)/(u^4 f^2), nonzero at interior beta/latitude. With k=2,beta=1/2,psi=pi/4,alpha=1/10, the respective values are5000/10251 and20000/40401. Direct differentiation gives the unchanged F1 coefficient c^2 cos^2(psi)/u^4-c^2 sin^2(psi)/u^2. The Laplacian is the trace of the corrected Hessian. The endpoint counterexample does not depend on this interior Hessian discrepancy.
problem_reviews.source_location: Actually viewed source24 and28-33; the decisive alpha^2 determinant/trace claim appears immediately after(122) on page33, while the fixed-base statement is on29 and the erroneous coefficients are(106)-(107) on31.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependencies: A false scaled determinant lower bound does not show Ricci nonpositivity. The source calls this simultaneous deformation the key delicate step and uses it to close Proposition6.7 within the main equivariant-twisting proof, justifying Major despite a local repair. No claim is made that all eigenvalues, the proposition itself, or the main manifold fail.
problem_reviews.repair_and_limits: Independently expanding the corrected components with q=c sin(psi) yields A=2+q^2+O_k(alpha^2), alpha B=-q+O_k(alpha^2), alpha^2 C=1+O_k(alpha^2). In the vertical entry the leading -2c^2 cos^2 term from the Laplacian cancels the +2c^2 cos^2 curvature term. The leading mixed term comes from the alpha^-2 term in(85). After removing the displayed alpha powers, all coefficients have smooth limits and denominators involving f,u>=1 on compact beta/psi ranges. Thus C-1>0 and the Schur complement of R-I equals A-1-(alpha B)^2/(alpha^2 C-alpha^2)=1+O_k(alpha^2), uniformly positive for small alpha. Coordinate-pole bounds extend by continuity. Z2,Z3 tend to2 and F1 has dominant alpha^-2 with uniformly bounded remaining terms. This verifies the local positivity repair from the stated base/connection formulas, not every later deformation or inherited gluing.

problem_reviews.claim: Coprimality and nonzero first weight do not imply freeness of the asserted circle subgroup on the stipulated product end.
problem_reviews.definitions_quantifiers_hypotheses: Proposition2.1(3)-(4) on page8 specifies a Hopf action on S3, an axial rotation on S2 in the end, and coprime integers(a,b) with a nonzero. Take(2,1), which satisfies both arithmetic conditions, and theta=pi, a nonidentity element of S1.
problem_reviews.decisive_evidence: At either S2 pole the second factor is fixed for every rotation, while the first factor is multiplied by exp(2i pi)=1. Therefore theta=pi fixes every end point with that pole, giving a nontrivial stabilizer under an allowed embedding.
problem_reviews.source_location: Actual source page8 Proposition2.1(3)-(4), base-step action and Theorem2.2; complete source text page7 describes the actual background model as S3 times a slightly curved R3.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependencies: The induction uses(1,k) and(1,0); the first weight is1. In the actual product construction the second circle acts only on R3, so it cannot cancel the first Hopf action on S3. The false extra generality is not needed for these actions.
problem_reviews.impact: Minor auxiliary overstatement, without an obstruction to the required induction.
problem_reviews.repair_and_limits: Restrict to a=+/-1 for the actual product model, or state the correct stabilizers. Necessity follows from the polar end points; sufficiency follows from the separately acting product factors described on source page7. The report's reference to the globally free first Hopf action is interpreted in this explicit product setting. Freeness of one factor alone would not prove this claim for an arbitrary torus action, and no such general inference is made.

problem_reviews.claim: Proposition4.4 cannot have the asserted exact volume equality for every eta>0.
problem_reviews.definitions_quantifiers_hypotheses: Actual page18 quantifies every eta>0 and imposes vol(B_ti(p))=t_i^(3+eta) on an unbounded sequence. It invokes the smooth complete dimension6 Ricci-nonnegative manifold of Theorem1.1, whose full source statement was read on page1.
problem_reviews.decisive_evidence: Choose eta=4. The primary comparison argument uses the radial shape-operator trace inequality m'+m^2/5<=0, m~5/r, hence m<=5/r and polar Jacobian at most r^5 up to the cut locus. Completeness permits integration over minimizing radial intervals, giving vol(B_t)<=omega6 t^6 with omega6=pi^3/6. Equality to t^7 is impossible for t>omega6, hence on any unbounded sequence. This is an exact necessary bound, not a numerical-only curvature claim.
problem_reviews.source_location: Actual source page18 Proposition4.4 and(31), compared with the complete extracted Theorem1.1 on source page1.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependencies: The main theorem asks for upper/lower inequalities, not exact equalities at every positive exponent. Oscillating growth exponents alone do not refute Bishop-Gromov monotonicity when scales and coefficients vary.
problem_reviews.impact: Minor overstatement of an auxiliary quantifier; no contradiction to the main weaker volume assertions is shown.
problem_reviews.repair_and_limits: Use a small-exponent range, for example0<eta0<1. For an arbitrary desired eta choose eta0<min(eta,1): at radii>=1, t^(3+eta0)<=t^(3+eta) and s^(6-eta0)>=s^(6-eta), which supplies the desired weaker inequalities. This verifies the logical reduction only; existence of the small-eta sequences remains a construction dependency.
